RLWRLD plans a public drink-handover and container-collection trial

TMIP and Mitsubishi Estate will support an October 15–16 trial in Otemachi to examine operation and public acceptance around people.

TMIP / PR TIMES ↗8 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 5

Two days in an urban setting

RLWRLD, Mitsubishi Estate and TMIP announced a trial for October 15–16 in Tokyo’s Otemachi Nakadori. Robots will hand drinks to participants and retrieve empty containers from designated positions on a table. Announced on October 8, the project is a planned trial, not a completed performance evaluation.

Technology and site responsibilities

RLWRLD provides robots running its RLDX-1 model, validates motions beforehand and handles on-site operation, monitoring and safety. Mitsubishi Estate coordinates the location and public access, while TMIP designs and manages the project. The partners aim to study operational feasibility and social acceptance in a shared human–robot environment.

Results remain to be established

The demonstration takes place during Wellness Weeks but only on the two specified days. Content may change following preliminary checks, weather or equipment conditions. No quantitative outcome is available yet. Collecting containers from designated positions does not demonstrate unrestricted cleanup capability or commercial readiness.
